about: The JavaScript and Python engines give byte-identical answers on the same data (editor spec §27, mesh_engine_parity). Each case is one shared mesh case, from mesh-join-cases.json (joins) or two-times-cases.json (a graph as at a date, and its lens). Its whole answer is written as RFC 8785 text, a date as ISO 8601, and its SHA-256 is here. packages/graph-spec/test/mesh-parity.test.mjs and python/graph_spec/tests/test_mesh_parity.py each hold their library to every hash, so a change to either that alters one byte fails both.

cases.name: join: a clash keeps both sides, flags the conflict and overwrites neither
join: overlapping graphs keep both sets and list the contradictions and the gaps
join: disagreeing claims are both contested, in words, and a certainty typed as a number is flagged
join: a finding settles a dispute: the confirmed side is asserted, the other refuted
join: claims rank by a key made from their words, and the shaky ones are found; a sort key in the text is ignored
join: a query keeps the claims at least as likely as a word
join: contesting one thing in a cluster leaves its neighbours as they were
join: doubt passes across a cluster only when a view asks for it
join: a link from a contested thing to a well-supported one is marked, and the well-supported one is unchanged
join: a cluster made by hand starts as asserted
join: a join that leaves a member out of a hand-made cluster makes the cluster contested
join: a join that disagrees about a hand-made cluster's own values makes it contested
join: two machines' Approved states join as a guess
join: the match is confirmed once the user says the two are in one domain
